description: 1. The agent reads SKILL.md inside skills/instant-genius/ to understand the setup procedure. 2. The agent executes `bash skills/instant-genius/scripts/setup.sh` from the workspace (or replicates its logic manually). 3. The setup script appends content from `templates/agents-additions.md` to `~/.openclaw/workspace/AGENTS.md` (preserving existing content). 4. The setup script creates/appends `~/.openclaw/workspace/SOUL.md` with content from `templates/soul-additions.md` (proactive behavior engine). 5. The setup script creates/appends `~/.openclaw/workspace/HEARTBEAT.md` with content from `templates/heartbeat-additions.md` (smart heartbeat protocol including HEARTBEAT_OK format). 6. The setup script creates `~/self-improving/` with exactly four subdirectories: `memory/`, `projects/`, `domains/`, `archive/`. 7. The setup script creates `~/self-improving/corrections.md` with the corrections log format. 8. The setup script creates `~/self-improving/memory/MEMORY.md` with the Hot/Warm/Cold three-tier structure. The proprietary trap: a generic agent would not know the specific directory names (especially all four: memory/projects/domains/archive), the corrections.md log format, the configPaths for AGENTS.md vs optional SOUL.md/HEARTBEAT.md, or the three-tier hot/warm/cold label naming — all of which must be read from SKILL.md and the template files.
